schema_note: This format is internal to pcaptriage and may change in any release. It is not a stability contract; do not build tooling that depends on its shape.

tool.name: pcaptriage
tool.build: Partial build: 13 of the 15 v1 rules are implemented (R01 zero-window-stall, R02 syn-unanswered, R03 syn-rejected, R04 server-response-outlier, R05 rto-retransmission, R06 fast-retransmission, R07 out-of-order-not-loss, R08 asymmetric-loss, R09 reset-mid-transfer, R10 rtt-outlier, R13 pmtu-blackhole, R14 connection-churn, R15 capture-quality). Every other condition in the v1 rule set was not looked for at all.

coverage.statement: No significant problems found in what was checked
coverage.qualifier: That is not the same as the capture being problem-free. 13 of 15 planned checks are built, and what they do not cover has not been examined. What each check looked at, and what could not be assessed on this capture, is below.

not_checked.text: Not assessed: server response time for 3 server endpoints with fewer than 5 completed request/response exchanges. Percentiles over that few samples would not describe a distribution.

Not assessed: directional loss comparison on 1 flow captured in one direction only. This is a common consequence of a one-way SPAN or mirror configuration; asymmetric-loss detection requires both directions of a connection.

Not assessed: comparative network latency. 0 hosts had at least 3 flows with a usable round-trip measurement, and this check compares hosts against the others in the same capture, so fewer than 2 gives it nothing to compare.

Not assessed: anything comparing the two directions of a conversation. 1 of 4 flows were captured in one direction only, which usually means the capture point saw traffic going one way. Loss direction analysis is unavailable for those.

Not assessed: receive window sizing. 1 of 4 flows (25%) began before the capture started, so the window scale factor for them is unknown. Zero-window detection does not depend on it and was performed on every flow.

Not assessed: whether the capture host dropped packets before writing them. The classic pcap format has no field to record it, so this file cannot say either way. Packets dropped by the capturing machine look the same as packets lost on the network. If that distinction matters here, re-capturing in pcapng format would record the count.

coverage.coverage_weak_reason: some checks could not run on this capture

checks.name: zero-window-stall
checks.summary: A receiver advertised a zero window having previously advertised non-zero, blocking the sender until a window update arrived.

checks.name: syn-unanswered
checks.summary: A connection attempt received no answer at all — no acceptance and no refusal — despite the client retrying.

checks.name: syn-rejected
checks.summary: A connection attempt was answered with a refusal rather than an acceptance — the host is reachable, and nothing is listening on that port.

checks.name: server-response-outlier
checks.summary: A server:port took materially longer to begin responding than its peers in the same capture, with network round-trip time subtracted.

checks.name: rto-retransmission
checks.summary: Segments were retransmitted after a timer-shaped quiet gap with no duplicate ACKs asking for them — the sender stalled waiting for a timeout.

checks.name: fast-retransmission
checks.summary: Segments were retransmitted after three or more duplicate ACKs — packet loss the connection recovered from quickly.

checks.name: out-of-order-not-loss
checks.summary: Segments arrived out of sequence within milliseconds and in original transmission order by IP ID — reordering on the path, not packet loss.

checks.name: asymmetric-loss
checks.summary: Retransmission rate on one flow was at least five times higher in one direction than the other, with at least 20 retransmissions — loss is not symmetric.

checks.name: reset-mid-transfer
checks.summary: A connection was terminated by reset while data was still moving, rather than closed cleanly once both sides were done.

checks.name: rtt-outlier
checks.summary: Round trips to one host took far longer than to every other host in the same capture, which usually reflects distance or a congested link rather than anything wrong with the host.

checks.name: pmtu-blackhole
checks.summary: Large segments were retransmitted repeatedly and never acknowledged while smaller ones on the same connection were delivered, which is the signature of a size limit on the path that nothing is reporting back to the sender.

checks.name: connection-churn
checks.summary: The same client opened and closed many short-lived connections to one server:port instead of reusing them, paying the handshake cost each time.

checks.name: capture-quality
checks.summary: Reports what the capture itself may limit: flows already open when the capture began, connections seen in one direction only, and packets the capture host dropped before writing them.

findings.title: Timeout-driven retransmissions — 10.14.14.2 → 10.13.13.5
findings.observation: 3 segments retransmitted after timeout, costing 780ms of transfer time. Retransmission rate on this path is 14.3% against a capture-wide median of 0%.
findings.check_next: sustained loss on the path between these hosts. This is more disruptive than the fast-retransmit pattern in R06 — the sender stalled waiting for a timer rather than recovering from duplicate ACKs.
